title: "Voltage divider"
subtitle: "Electrical engineering basics"

## Unloaded divider

Two resistors in series across a supply split the voltage in proportion to resistance:

$$
V_{out} = V_{in} \cdot \frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}
$$

## Loaded divider

Once something draws current from the output node — an ADC input, another circuit — that load resistor $R_L$ sits in parallel with $R_2$, and the divider ratio changes:

$$
V_{out} = V_{in} \cdot \frac{R_2 \| R_L}{R_1 + (R_2 \| R_L)}, \qquad R_2 \| R_L = \frac{R_2 R_L}{R_2 + R_L}
$$

This is why a divider that measures correctly open-circuit can read low once connected to a real load — the rule of thumb is to keep $R_L \gg R_2$, typically 10× or more.

## Calculator

Set load resistance very high (default) to see the unloaded case.

```{=html}
<div id="vdiv-calc"></div>
<script>
Calc.create({
  root: "vdiv-calc",
  inputs: [
    { id: "Vin", label: "Vin (V)", value: 5, min: 0, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "R1", label: "R1 (Ω)", value: 1000, min: 0.01, step: 10 },
    { id: "R2", label: "R2 (Ω)", value: 1000, min: 0.01, step: 10 },
    { id: "RL", label: "Load RL (Ω)", value: 1000000, min: 0.01, step: 100 }
  ],
  outputs: [
    { id: "vout", label: "Vout" },
    { id: "r2eff", label: "R2 || RL" }
  ],
  compute: function (v) {
    if (v.R1 <= 0 || v.R2 <= 0 || v.RL <= 0) return { vout: "-", r2eff: "-" };
    var r2eff = (v.R2 * v.RL) / (v.R2 + v.RL);
    var vout = v.Vin * (r2eff / (v.R1 + r2eff));
    return {
      vout: vout.toFixed(3) + " V",
      r2eff: r2eff.toFixed(1) + " Ω"
    };
  }
});
</script>
```
